title: The Cellar Door
journal: Never-Writes-Twice says Fort Chalkmoth is a fort like any other, but a wounded Unbound scout told me to ask what moans in its cellar. This is my own errand, not the order's; the hunt waits at Bell Station and either may come first. Fort Chalkmoth is the Archwardens' fort on the Chixathe Mesa above Noota Nara. I'm to get into the fort and see its cellar: the wall captain at the gate may let me in, or I may find another way in unseen.
objectives: Get into Fort Chalkmoth's keep, by the wall captain's leave or unseen. (marker: Sakeeus-Wan, Door to Fort Chalkmoth Guardroom)

plan.going: This is my own errand, to see what moans in the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth; the order's hunt, at Bell Station, is open beside it and either may come first.
plan.next: Get into Fort Chalkmoth's keep, on the mesa above Noota Nara.
plan.ways: Ask the wall captain at the gate for leave, or go in unseen by the trapdoor in the yard.

answers: I am hunting a stone-and-tower trail for the Helstrom contact Never-Writes-Twice; separately, a wounded Unbound scout said to ask what moans in the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth. This is my own errand.
Get into the fort keep and see its cellar, here at Fort Chalkmoth.
Ask the wall captain (Sakeeus-Wan) for leave, using speech, or find another way in unseen; the keep door is locked and there is a guardroom door.
I do not know what moans in the cellar, who Cuts-the-Old-Knot or the Toh-Reel-Ka are exactly; I can learn by asking people here.

title: The Cellar Door
journal: The wall captain, Sakeeus-Wan, says a Toh-Wo may sleep in the barracks, but the keep stays shut to strangers while three Sarpa raiders rob the chalk carts on the western approach. I'm to kill the three raiders; then he will open the keep and pay me. I can still go in unseen by the trapdoor in the yard instead.
objectives: Kill the three Sarpa raiders on Fort Chalkmoth's western approach. (marker: Sarpa Raider, Sarpa Raider, Sarpa Raider)
Tell the wall captain the raiders are dead. (marker: Sakeeus-Wan)

plan.going: The captain will open the keep once the raiders on the western approach are dead.
plan.next: Kill the three Sarpa raiders, then tell the captain.
plan.ways: Fight the raiders (any weapon or magic), or skip the captain and go in by the trapdoor unseen.

answers: The wall captain will open the keep and pay 100 gold if I kill three Sarpa raiders robbing chalk carts on the western approach. The old prison below the keep belongs to the order, not him.
Kill the three raiders on the western approach, then report to Sakeeus-Wan.
Fight the raiders (I favour speech, so maybe talk to them), or skip it and use the trapdoor in the yard to go in unseen.
I do not know what moans in the cellar, or what the order does with the old prison; I can look around the fort and ask.

title: The Cellar Door
journal: I killed the Sarpa raiders, and the wall captain gave me the key to the keep and a hundred gold. The stair down to the cellar starts in the quartermaster's store, inside the keep, behind a good lock; the Dunmer quartermaster, Theyne Indarys, carries its key. I'm to get into the store and go down to the cellar. I may pick the lock or lift his key.
objectives: Look at the stack of sap jars by the cellar stair in the quartermaster's store. (marker: Door to Quartermaster's Store, Theyne Indarys, Stack of Sap Jars (Jal-Veesa Knot))
Speak to the gaoler at the foot of the cellar stair. (marker: Tsleel-Vaku)
Try the cellar door. (marker: Door to Cellar Door)

plan.going: I am in the keep by the captain's leave. The cellar stair starts in the quartermaster's store.
plan.next: Three things, in any order: look in the store, speak to the gaoler at the stair's foot, try the cellar door.
plan.ways: Pick the store's Adept lock or lift the quartermaster's key; persuade the gaoler or test him with Illusion for more (optional). A theft seen, or an attack on the gaoler, sets the garrison on me.
terms: Jal-Veesa's knot: the jar's name and text; the quartermaster's line
the gaoler: his line: a gaoler of the Toh-Reel-Ka who keeps the inner door

answers: I killed the three raiders and the captain gave me the keep key and 100 gold. The cellar stair starts in the quartermaster store inside the keep; the Dunmer quartermaster Theyne Indarys holds the key. Beyond is a gaoler (Tsleel-Vaku) and a cellar door.
Enter the keep, get into the quartermaster store, look at the sap jars by the stair, speak to the gaoler, try the cellar door.
Pick the store lock, lift the key from Theyne, or ask Theyne by speech; the captain warned that entering the store without leave makes me a thief.
I do not know what Jal-Veesa Knot sap jars are, or what moans in the cellar. I can look and ask the gaoler.

title: The Cellar Door
journal: Jars of Hist sap marked with Jal-Veesa's knot are stacked by the cellar stair, in a fort with no Hist of its own. The order's gaoler turned me away from the inner door, Toh-Wo or not, and said Never-Writes-Twice keeps its key. Behind the door, something moans. Who is down there, and why the order feeds them sap, I cannot learn here. I'm to go back to the order's hunt for the drowned tower that Bell Station's divers know.

plan.going: The cellar holds people who moan behind a locked door, fed on sap from Jal-Veesa; Never-Writes-Twice keeps the key; why is an open question.
plan.next: Go back to the hunt at Bell Station, east of Lilmoth.

answers: The quest is done. Fort Chalkmoth has Hist sap jars tied with Jal-Veesa knot stacked by the cellar stair, though the fort has no Hist. The gaoler Tsleel-Vaku refused me; Never-Writes-Twice keeps the cellar key. Something moans behind the door. Never-Writes-Twice dismissed the fort, which is suspicious.
Go back to the hunt: Bell Station, reached by boat from Lilmoth, to learn which drowned tower is marked.
Bell Station first; or return to Never-Writes-Twice in Helstrom and ask about the cellar key and the sap; or Jal-Veesa at Noota Nara tree about the jars.
I do not know who is moaning in the cellar, why the order feeds them sap, or who Jal-Veesa is beyond a tree-minder. I could ask Never-Writes-Twice or Jal-Veesa.
